I don’t think so. I mean, people say I “go on” about things, sure, because they don’t want to hear the whole explanation. They want me to answer everything in two words, and some things don’t fit into two words. If I’m trying to explain what happened or why something doesn’t add up, I have to include the parts that connect, otherwise they act like I’m just making accusations out of nowhere.

But hard to follow? I don’t know. Nobody has really said it like that to me. They might get impatient or say, “You’re not making sense,” but I think that’s more because they don’t like what I’m saying, not because I’m jumping around for no reason. I know what I mean when I’m talking. Sometimes I have to back up and explain the beginning, then the middle, because people keep interrupting or pretending they don’t understand.

So… no, I haven’t noticed my speech being hard to follow like that. People just don’t listen right.

I mean… yes, but it’s mostly connected to the money. It’s not like I walk around thinking every stranger is after me or something. It’s people who are involved, or who know what’s going on and won’t admit it. My family and some friends keep acting like I’m making it up because they say the bank papers don’t show anything was taken, but those papers don’t explain everything. For over a year I’ve known they’ve been hiding my money. Why keep making it look like the money went toward normal things?

That’s why I keep confronting them. I know everyone says I should stop bringing it up, but I can’t just let people lie to my face and then tell me I’m the problem. I’m not saying someone is going to jump out and hurt me, but I do believe they’re working together to keep the truth from me until I get tired and drop it. And I’m not going to, because I need them to finally tell the truth.

No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or unusually irritable for days at a time?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, I get irritated, yes, but anybody would be irritated if people kept acting like you’re crazy when you’re just asking questions. I need them to finally admit what they did.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?\n\nPatient: No… I mean, not like that. I don’t sit in a room and hear somebody talking when nobody’s there, if that’s what you mean. People keep trying to make it sound like I’m hearing things or imagining things, but that’s not what’s happening.\n\nWhat I’m talking about is what people say to me and what they do, the way they act, the way they change the story. I hear them just fine when they’re actually there. But voices out of nowhere? No, I haven’t noticed anything like that.\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or unusually irritable for days at a time?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, I get irritated, yes, but anybody would be irritated if people kept acting like you’re crazy when you’re just asking questions. So if you mean have I been in some kind of happy, excited mood for days, like feeling on top of the world or something, no, I don’t think so.\n\nI’ve had days where I’m worked up because I’m thinking about everything and trying to get people to stop lying to me, but that’s not the same as being in some strange high mood. It’s more like frustration, because I keep getting pushed into defending myself. So… unusually high, no. Irritable, maybe, but I think there’s a reason for it.\n\nDoctor: Is it possible that you might be mistaken about your family stealing your money?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think I’m mistaken. I know people keep wanting me to say that, like if I just admit maybe I’m wrong then everybody can stop talking about it and pretend everything is fine. But it isn’t fine.\n\nI’ve been watching this for over a year. It’s not like I woke up one morning and just decided my family was stealing from me. It’s the way they explain things, the way money is suddenly tied up in bills, or somebody has a fundraiser, or there’s some trip being talked about, and then when I ask where my money is or why something doesn’t add up, they shove bank papers at me like that proves everything. But papers don’t tell the whole story. People can hide things behind papers.\n\nAnd my friends are doing it too, or at least they keep backing them up, saying, “Nothing was taken, look at the records,” like I’m stupid. I’m not stupid. I know when people are covering for each other. So no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken. I think they want me to doubt myself so I’ll stop confronting them. But I’m not going to stop until they tell the truth.\n\nDoctor: Before all of this with the money, have you generally tended to distrust other people?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, what do you mean by “distrust”? Because I don’t think I walked around thinking everybody was out to get me or anything like that, if that’s what you’re asking. I’ve always been the kind of person who watches how people act, maybe, and I don’t just believe every word somebody says because people do lie sometimes. That’s just life.\n\nBut before all this, I don’t know that I would’ve called myself a suspicious person. I wasn’t sitting there keeping score on everybody. I had people around me, I talked to people. I guess I could be careful with people if something didn’t feel right, but I don’t think that’s the same as distrusting everybody. It’s hard to answer because now everybody acts like anything I say means I had some problem all along, and I don’t think that’s fair.\n\nDoctor: During this past year, have you had a period where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?\n\nPatient: I don’t know if I’d call it depressed most of the day nearly every day. I mean, I’ve been upset a lot, yes. There are days where I wake up already tired of having to think about all this, and I feel worn down because it’s like nobody listens to me and everybody wants to turn it around on me. But depressed like… just sad all day for no reason, every day? I’m not sure that’s what it is.\n\nIt’s more like I get angry, or hurt, or exhausted from having to keep explaining myself. Some days I don’t feel like dealing with people because I already know what they’re going to say. But I don’t know how to separate that from what’s been going on. If people were treating me honestly, I don’t think I’d feel this way.\n\nSo… I guess I’ve had bad days, a lot of stress, but I can’t say there was one clear period where I was depressed nearly every day all day. Not like that.\n\nDoctor: Have other people told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense to them?\n\nPatient: I don’t think so. I mean, people say I “go on” about things, sure, because they don’t want to hear the whole explanation. They want me to answer everything in two words, and some things don’t fit into two words. If I’m trying to explain what happened or why something doesn’t add up, I have to include the parts that connect, otherwise they act like I’m just making accusations out of nowhere.\n\nBut hard to follow? I don’t know. Nobody has really said it like that to me. They might get impatient or say, “You’re not making sense,” but I think that’s more because they don’t like what I’m saying, not because I’m jumping around for no reason. I know what I mean when I’m talking. Sometimes I have to back up and explain the beginning, then the middle, because people keep interrupting or pretending they don’t understand.\n\nSo… no, I haven’t noticed my speech being hard to follow like that. People just don’t listen right.\n\nDoctor: Have you felt that other people can read your thoughts?\n\nPatient: Read my thoughts? No… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t know how that would even work, exactly. Sometimes people act like they know what I’m going to say before I say it, or they jump in and assume what I mean, and that bothers me because it’s like they’ve already decided what I’m thinking. But that’s not the same as actually reading my thoughts, I guess.\n\nI’ve had people look at me a certain way, like they think they’ve got me figured out, and I’ll be sitting there thinking, “You don’t know what’s in my head.” But I wouldn’t say I feel like they can literally hear my thoughts or anything like that. It’s more that people make assumptions and then treat those assumptions like facts. So… no, not really.\n\nDoctor: Aside from your family and friends hiding your money, have you believed that anyone else was trying to harm you or plot against you?\n\nPatient: I mean… yes, but it’s mostly connected to the money. It’s not like I walk around thinking every stranger is after me or something. It’s people who are involved, or who know what’s going on and won’t admit it. My family and some friends keep acting like I’m making it up because they say the bank papers don’t show anything was taken, but those papers don’t explain everything. But I don’t think I’ve lost interest in everything or anything like that.\n\nSo… no, not really. Not that I’ve noticed.\n\nDoctor: During this past year, have there been times when you were much more active than usual, constantly taking on tasks or pursuing plans?\n\nPatient: Much more active than usual? No… not really like the TV or radio is talking to me or sending me secret messages. That’s not what I mean when I say something is going on.

It’s more about my family and people around me, and the money.
